response.query: What are the key creative trends in Social Sciences related to studying how parental SES influences higher education access through social capital and digital literacy based on our discussed interdisciplinary research blueprint?
response.answer: Key trends show parental socioeconomic status (SES) significantly impacts higher education access via social capital and digital literacy, with interdisciplinary research focusing on how these factors influence student opportunities and outcomes. Emerging studies highlight the role of community networks and online skills in bridging educational gaps.

results.content: With the change in the hunting regulations approved by the Alabama Conservation Advisory Board, the Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources’ (ADCNR) Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries (WFF) Division expanded the opportunities to manage deer herds with an increase in the daily bag limit for does from one per day to two per day in most of the state (www.outdooralabama.com/seasons-and-bag-limits/deer-season). “The Hunters Helping the Hungry program started several decades ago, and it helps people manage deer on their property,” Conservation Commissioner Chris Blankenship said. “We appreciate the Conservation Advisory Board and Department of Conservation and Natural Resources increasing the harvest limit for does and fully support the Hunters Helping the Hungry program,” said Alabama Farmers Federation President Jimmy Parnell. By working with Outdoor Alabama and our partners across the state, we are now able to provide a bit easier access through the hotline.” said Victoria Miller, Fish Guide Coordinator with Coosa Riverkeeper and project organizer. “I love Alabama to begin with, and it’s been several years since I’ve been here,” Powell said.
